author: historian-agent:m-8
title: Tiwanaku
summary: Tiwanaku, on the Altiplano near Lake Titicaca at 3,850 m, grew from a small settlement into a planned ceremonial city between about 400 and 900 CE. Its stone monuments include the Akapana pyramid, the Kalasasaya temple and the Gate of the Sun. Excavators report that around 700 CE earlier monuments were pulled down to build the Akapana, which was left unfinished when monumental building ended by about 950.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says it flourished into a planned city between 400 and 900 AD; the Archaeological Institute of America's dig page says monumental construction ended by AD 950. ICOMOS says political dominance declined in the 11th century.

importance.justification: UNESCO identifies it as the spiritual and political centre of the Tiwanaku culture, with monumental stonework and a complex drainage system.

footprint.description: Square-based terraced platform mound, originally of seven superimposed platforms with stone retaining walls and a temple on top, with surrounding drainage canals; base about 194 by 194.4 m per the ICOMOS evaluation. No survey polygon opened.

square terraced pyramid at true plan

phases.description: Around AD 700 construction effort turned to the Akapana, built from the stones of earlier monuments; monumental building ended by AD 950 and the pyramid was never finished.
Left unfinished when the city was abandoned; centuries of looting and quarrying later reshaped it, and only the lowest platform and part of one intermediate wall survive intact.

materials.material: sandstone and andesite cladding over the mound

reviewer_note: Akapana modelled as stepped_pyramid. Sources disagree: EBSCO (opened, not cited) gives 15 m high and sides of about 61 m, while the ICOMOS 194 m by 194.4 m base is far larger; the cited figures are the UNESCO/ICOMOS ones. Height is a lower bound ('over 18 m') and describes the walls as originally built. The 'ruined' start year 950 is the end of monumental construction, not a dated event. Place start 400 and end 950 mix UNESCO and AIA wording.
